title: Two-generator regular-sequence blowup atlas and Cartier equations
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, and let $x,y\in A$ be such that both $(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ are regular sequences. Put $I=(x,y)$, $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ and $Z=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Then the standard blowup charts give an open cover $Y=U_x\cup U_y$ with canonical $A$-algebra presentations
$$U_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_x,\quad C_x=A[I/x]\cong A[t]/(xt-y),\qquad U_y\cong\operatorname{Spec}C_y,\quad C_y=A[I/y]\cong A[u]/(yu-x).$$
The chart coordinate $t$ corresponds to $y/x$ in the subalgebra $A[I/x]\subseteq A_x$, and $u$ to $x/y$ in $A[I/y]\subseteq A_y$. In the Rees-algebra Proj description these charts are $D_+(xT)$ and $D_+(yT)$, and their coordinates are $(yT)/(xT)$ and $(xT)/(yT)$. The rings $C_x,C_y$ are Noetherian. Their extended ideals are $IC_x=(x)$ and $IC_y=(y)$, and multiplication by $x$ on $C_x$ and by $y$ on $C_y$ is injective. The closed subscheme $Z$ is defined on these charts by these extended ideals, so $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact.
Conventions: [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], [def-nagata-affine-proj], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Further construction conventions: [def-nagata-affine-blowup], [def-nagata-rees-algebra], [def-weil-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] to the generating list $(x,y)$ of $I$. This gives the open cover by $U_x=\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/x])$ and $U_y=\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/y])$. In the affine Proj model [def-nagata-affine-blowup], the maps of [def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map] identify these with $D_+(xT)$ and $D_+(yT)$: [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart] says precisely that those chart maps are isomorphisms over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus the ring structures on the two charts are the structural $A$-algebra structures, not merely abstract ring structures.

Apply [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] first with $(a,a_2)=(x,y)$ and then with $(a,a_2)=(y,x)$. The respective regular-sequence hypotheses are both explicitly assumed. The two resulting canonical $A$-algebra isomorphisms give $C_x\cong A[t]/(xt-y)$ with $t\mapsto y/x$, and $C_y\cong A[u]/(yu-x)$ with $u\mapsto x/y$. Under the chart morphisms in step 1, [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart] sends $(yT)/(xT)$ to $y/x$ and $(xT)/(yT)$ to $x/y$, by its displayed formula with $n=1$. This verifies the specified Proj coordinates as well as the hypersurface presentations.

source.place: Tag 0BIQ, lemma-blowup-regular-sequence, applied to both orderings; chart-fraction convention of Tag 0804

proof.text: The presentations in step 2 exhibit each $C_x,C_y$ as a quotient of a polynomial algebra in one variable over the Noetherian ring $A$. In particular these are finite type $A$-algebras in exactly the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Apply that statement twice to conclude that both chart rings are Noetherian. No regular-local or domain hypothesis on $A$ is used.

Apply [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] with $a=x$ and $a=y$ to obtain $IC_x=(x)$ and $IC_y=(y)$. Apply [lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular] to the same two chart rings: multiplication by $x$ on $C_x$ and by $y$ on $C_y$ is injective. These statements concern the structural images of the indicated elements. They also follow directly from the fraction model: $y=xt$ and $x=yu$ give the two ideal equalities, and cancellation by $x$ in $A_x$ or by $y$ in $A_y$ restricts to injectivity on the respective subalgebras.

source.place: Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), proof of (2), citing algebra.tex Tag 07Z3 (lemma-affine-blowup)

proof.text: For either chart ring $C$, the fibre product description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its part of $Z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}((A/I)\otimes_A C)$, the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ being induced by $c\mapsto\bar1\otimes c$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] identifies this module with $C/IC$, by $\bar a\otimes c\mapsto ac\bmod IC$. This is also an isomorphism of rings: it takes $\bar1\otimes1$ to $1$ and the product $(\bar a\otimes c)(\bar b\otimes d)$ to $abcd\bmod IC$, the product of the images; additive extension gives the assertion for sums. Hence the chart projection is the closed subscheme defined by $IC$, by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. With step 4 these ideals are $(x)$ on $U_x$ and $(y)$ on $U_y$.

source.place: Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), proof of (2); schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); algebra.tex Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact)

proof.text: The extended ideal on the cover $U_x\cup U_y$ therefore defines $Z$ and is generated there by the nonzerodivisors in step 4. This is exactly the open-cover criterion in [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Thus $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $Y$.

The two Noetherian affine chart rings of step 3 give a locally Noetherian affine cover of $Y$, so [pqf-def-locnoeth] gives local Noetherianity. By clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], each of $U_x,U_y$ is quasi-compact. Any open cover of $Y$ restricts to an open cover of each chart; choose a finite subcover of each chart and take the union of the two finite index sets. This is a finite subcover of $Y$. Thus $Y$ is also quasi-compact, which is the stipulated meaning of Noetherian.
